For most people the best DHM supplement is [NusaPure DHM 1,000 mg](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08B32XBRB?tag=dhmguide-20): 1,000 mg of dihydromyricetin (DHM) per serving, nothing else in it, and $0.48 a serving, the lowest price per milligram of the eight we compare. [Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) is the same dose at $0.80 with far more reviews. [DHM Depot](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0767N448Q?tag=dhmguide-20) is the pick if you want to start at 300 mg. If you want one product that adds L-cysteine and electrolytes, [No Days Wasted DHM Detox](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) is the most complete, at about four times the price per milligram.

Buy on dose and price rather than marketing. DHM has mostly animal and lab research behind it, and no brand has shown in a human trial that it prevents hangovers.

We ranked each product on the DHM dose per serving, the listed price, the number of servings, and the price per 100 mg of DHM, which is the fairest way to compare a 300 mg capsule with a 1,000 mg one. We didn't run lab tests. We also looked at what else is in each formula and whether those extras make sense. Prices change often on Amazon, so treat the figures below as a snapshot. Our [DHM supplement reviews](/reviews) show the same products with ratings, and the [comparison tool](/compare) puts any two side by side.

> **This is not medical advice.** DHM is a dietary supplement. Supplements are not reviewed by the FDA for safety or effectiveness before they're sold. **Talk to your doctor or pharmacist before taking DHM if** you take prescription medicines (especially sedatives, sleep medicines, anti-anxiety drugs, blood thinners, or drugs processed by the liver), you are pregnant or breastfeeding, you have liver or kidney disease, or you're under 21. No supplement makes it safe to drive after drinking or to drink more than you otherwise would.

The cheapest DHM here costs about a nickel per 100 mg and the most expensive more than a dollar, roughly a 25-fold gap for the same main ingredient. ## What Is a DHM Supplement?

DHM stands for **dihydromyricetin**, a flavonoid (a type of plant compound) found in several plants. Commercial DHM is usually extracted from **vine tea** (*Ampelopsis grossedentata*), which is naturally rich in it. It's also associated with the **Japanese raisin tree** (*Hovenia dulcis*), which has a long history in traditional East Asian remedies for drinking. Our guide to the [Japanese raisin tree and DHM](/never-hungover/dhm-japanese-raisin-tree-complete-guide) covers the plant's history in more detail.

A DHM supplement is a capsule or tablet that delivers a measured amount of that compound. The products here fall into three groups. NusaPure, DHM Depot and Double Wood are plain DHM, usually 300 mg or 1,000 mg per serving. No Days Wasted, Cheers Restore and Flyby are DHM-led blends that add L-cysteine, milk thistle, prickly pear, B vitamins or electrolytes. Toniiq Ease is a liver-support stack that pairs DHM with reishi mushroom and milk thistle.

### A labeling trap to watch for: "Hovenia dulcis extract" is not the same as DHM

Some products list **Hovenia dulcis extract** or "Japanese raisin tree extract" rather than dihydromyricetin itself. That isn't automatically bad, but it isn't the same thing. An extract of the plant contains many compounds, and the label often doesn't say how much of it is actually DHM. If the supplement facts panel doesn't state a DHM amount in milligrams, you have no way to know what dose you're getting. All of the products in our table list DHM directly.

## Does DHM Actually Work? What the Research Supports

Most of the research on DHM comes from animals and lab work. Human evidence for hangovers specifically is thin.

**The rodent research that started the interest.** A widely cited 2012 study by Yi Shen, Jing Liang and colleagues at UCLA, published in the *Journal of Neuroscience* ([Shen et al., 2012](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22219299/)), found that injected DHM reduced signs of alcohol intoxication and withdrawal in rats. The proposed mechanism involves GABA-A receptors in the brain, the same receptors alcohol acts on. This study is the main reason DHM became a "hangover supplement," but it was done in rats, not people.

**Liver and alcohol metabolism in animals.** Later work, including mouse studies from the same research group after it moved to the University of Southern California, reported that DHM supported the enzymes that break down alcohol and its toxic by-product acetaldehyde, and reduced signs of alcohol-related liver stress. Again, promising, but in animals.

**The best human data is about the liver, not hangovers.** A randomized, placebo-controlled trial published in 2015 in *Pharmacological Research* ([Chen et al.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26032587/)) gave 60 people with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease 600 mg of DHM a day, or a placebo, for three months. The DHM group ended with lower liver enzymes, blood glucose and LDL cholesterol. It's encouraging for liver health, but it didn't test hangovers and didn't involve drinking.

**What's missing.** There are no large, independent human trials showing that DHM reliably reduces hangover symptoms. Many people report feeling better when they take it, and that experience counts for something, but it's hard to separate from other things people do on the same night, like drinking more water or pacing themselves. There's also evidence from animal studies that DHM is poorly absorbed when taken by mouth, which is one reason some brands pair it with other ingredients or use larger doses.

Our full breakdown is in [Does DHM work?](/never-hungover/does-dhm-work-honest-science-review-2025), and the human studies are summarized in our [DHM clinical trials guide](/never-hungover/dhm-randomized-controlled-trials). Treat DHM as a reasonable thing to try, not a guarantee. That is another reason to buy on value: if it turns out not to help you, you've lost less money.

## The Best DHM Supplements, Brand by Brand

All of these are sold on Amazon. We earn a small commission if you buy through our links, at no extra cost to you, and it doesn't change how we rank them.

### Best overall value: NusaPure DHM 1,000 mg

[NusaPure Dihydromyricetin 1,000 mg](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08B32XBRB?tag=dhmguide-20) is the plainest product here and, on current pricing, the cheapest per milligram by a wide margin. You get 60 servings of 1,000 mg DHM and nothing else.

**Pros**
- Lowest price per 100 mg of DHM in our comparison (about $0.05)
- 60 servings in one bottle, enough for months of occasional use
- Single ingredient, so you know exactly what you're taking

**Cons**
- Fewer customer reviews than the bigger brands
- No supporting ingredients, if you want those
- 1,000 mg per serving is more than some people need; there's no easy way to take a smaller dose

**Best for:** anyone who wants straightforward DHM at the lowest cost. More detail in our [NusaPure DHM review](/never-hungover/nusapure-dhm-review-analysis).

[Double Wood DHM](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) is one of the longest-running DHM products on Amazon and has a large base of reviews. It delivers 1,000 mg of DHM per serving at around $0.80 a serving.

**Pros**
- 1,000 mg DHM per serving
- About $0.08 per 100 mg, still very good value
- Large review history, so you're not the first person trying it

**Cons**
- Costs more per milligram than NusaPure
- No extra ingredients beyond DHM and minor minerals
- 30 servings per bottle, half the count of NusaPure

**Best for:** people who want a widely used, simple DHM product. See our [Double Wood DHM review](/never-hungover/double-wood-dhm-review-analysis), or the head-to-head [Double Wood vs NusaPure comparison](/never-hungover/double-wood-vs-nusapure-dhm-comparison-2025).

[DHM Depot](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0767N448Q?tag=dhmguide-20) sells 300 mg capsules, 50 to a bottle, at about $0.40 each.

**Pros**

- 300 mg capsules make it easy to adjust your dose up or down
- Single ingredient

**Cons**
- At 300 mg per serving, reaching 600 mg takes two servings ($0.80 a night), which erases the price advantage over the 1,000 mg brands
- Fewer extras and simpler branding than the premium options

**Best for:** people who prefer flexible, smaller doses, or who want to start low. Our [DHM Depot review](/never-hungover/dhm-depot-review-2025) has more.

## How to Choose a DHM Supplement: Five Things That Matter

Most "best DHM" lists rank products by star rating. Star ratings mostly measure packaging, shipping, and expectations. Here's what actually separates one DHM supplement from another.

### 1. The DHM dose in milligrams

Look for a clearly stated amount of **dihydromyricetin** on the supplement facts panel. If you only see a "proprietary blend" with a total weight, you don't know how much DHM is inside.

### 2. Price per 100 mg of DHM

This is the single most useful number for comparing brands. To work it out:

1. Divide the bottle price by the number of servings to get the price per serving.
2. Divide that by the DHM dose per serving, then multiply by 100.

For example, a $28.99 bottle with 60 servings of 1,000 mg costs about $0.48 a serving, which works out to roughly $0.05 per 100 mg.

### 3. Whether the extras are worth paying for

L-cysteine is an amino acid the body uses to make glutathione, an antioxidant the liver relies on. A Finnish trial of 19 men found that 1,200 mg was linked to less nausea and headache after drinking ([Eriksson et al., 2020](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32808029/)). That is one small study, and it was not testing DHM.

Milk thistle (silymarin) is the most researched liver herb. Human results are mixed, but it's generally well tolerated. See our [DHM vs milk thistle comparison](/never-hungover/dhm-vs-milk-thistle-which-liver-supplement-more-effective-2025).

Prickly pear has one older, small study suggesting it reduced some hangover symptoms. B vitamins and electrolytes are cheap to add and harmless at normal doses, but food and an electrolyte drink do the same job.

If you'd like these ingredients, a combination product is convenient. If you only want DHM, a single-ingredient product will save you a lot of money.

### 4. Capsule size and count per serving

Some formulas need three capsules for one serving. That matters if you dislike swallowing pills or want to carry a few in your wallet.

### 5. Manufacturing and testing

Look for products made in facilities that follow current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP). Third-party testing is a plus, though brands vary in how much detail they publish. Because supplements aren't approved by the FDA before sale, choosing an established brand with a clear label is the most practical safeguard you have.

## DHM Supplement Dosage: How Much to Take and When

There is no established human dose for DHM. Products mostly put 300 mg or 1,000 mg in a serving, and the fatty-liver study above, the one controlled human trial of DHM capsules we have found, used 600 mg a day. Start at 300 mg, go up if you want to, and stay within the label.

Nobody has tested timing in people either. Some people take a dose with their first drink, on the reasoning that DHM would need to be in the body while alcohol is. Others take it before bed with a glass of water. There's no strong human evidence favoring one over the other. Our [DHM dosage guide](/never-hungover/dhm-dosage-guide-2025) explains where the dose numbers come from and which product matches each amount.

## DHM Supplement Side Effects and Safety

DHM appears to be well tolerated in the studies done so far, and side effects reported by users are usually mild. That said, long-term human safety data is limited.

Reported or possible side effects include:

- Mild stomach upset or nausea
- Drowsiness, especially combined with alcohol
- Headache (which can be hard to separate from drinking itself)

Be more careful, and check with a doctor or pharmacist first, if you:

- take sedatives or sleep medicines. DHM acts on GABA-A receptors in animal studies, so combining it with benzodiazepines, sleep aids or other sedatives on top of alcohol could add to drowsiness.
- take diabetes medicine. DHM lowered blood glucose in the fatty-liver trial.
- take blood thinners or other medicines processed by the liver. Interaction data for DHM in people is limited.
- are pregnant or breastfeeding. There's no safety data, and alcohol should be avoided anyway.
- have liver or kidney disease.

Our [DHM safety guide](/never-hungover/dhm-safety-complete-guide-2025) and [DHM medication interactions guide](/never-hungover/dhm-medication-interactions-safety-guide-2025) cover this in more depth. If you plan to use it often, read [can you take DHM every day?](/never-hungover/can-you-take-dhm-every-day-long-term-guide-2025).

> **When to skip the supplement and get help.** DHM is meant for social drinkers trying to feel better the next day. It is not a treatment for alcohol poisoning or for withdrawal. Call 911 if someone who has been drinking is confused, can't stay awake, is vomiting while drowsy, has slow or irregular breathing, has a seizure, or has bluish or very pale skin. If you get shaky, sweaty, anxious, or have a racing heart when you stop drinking after several days of heavy use, that can be a sign of withdrawal, and it's worth talking to a doctor rather than treating it with supplements.

## DHM Capsules vs Powders vs Drinks

Most DHM is sold as capsules or tablets, which are the easiest to dose and carry because the amount is printed on the label. Powders are often cheaper per gram, but DHM tastes bitter and small doses are hard to measure without a scale. Drinks and shots are convenient at a party, but usually expensive per milligram, and many don't say how much DHM they contain.

There's no good evidence that one form is absorbed meaningfully better than another in people. Our [DHM product forms comparison](/never-hungover/dhm-product-forms-absorption-comparison-2025) covers the claims brands make about absorption.

## Where to Buy DHM Supplements

DHM is sold mainly online, through Amazon and brand websites. It's less common in pharmacies and grocery stores in the US, although some larger retailers carry one or two brands. Buying online usually gives you more choice and lower prices.

On Amazon, check that the seller is the brand itself or Amazon, which lowers the chance of counterfeit or old stock, and check the expiry date when the bottle arrives. Our guide to [where to buy DHM](/never-hungover/where-to-buy-dhm) covers which stores sometimes carry it. If you're outside the US, availability varies by country. Our [DHM availability worldwide guide](/never-hungover/dhm-availability-worldwide-guide-2025) covers where to find it.

## What a DHM Supplement Won't Do

It won't sober you up. There is no good evidence that DHM lowers blood alcohol in people by an amount that matters for safety, so never drive after drinking, whatever you've taken.

It won't undo heavy drinking either. How much you drink is still the biggest factor in how you feel the next day and in long-term liver health. Eating before you drink, alternating with water and stopping earlier all have better support than any supplement, and our guide on [how to prevent a hangover](/never-hungover/how-to-prevent-a-hangover) covers the habits with the best evidence.

## Our Bottom Line

If you want to try DHM, start with a simple, single-ingredient product and judge it on price per 100 mg of DHM. [NusaPure](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B08B32XBRB?tag=dhmguide-20) and [Double Wood](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B074N712FM?tag=dhmguide-20) give you full 1,000 mg doses for well under a dollar a serving, and [DHM Depot](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0767N448Q?tag=dhmguide-20) is a good pick if you'd rather start low. If you prefer one product with added L-cysteine and electrolytes and don't mind paying more, [No Days Wasted](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0D4BWK6PH?tag=dhmguide-20) is the most complete of the combination formulas.

To see every brand with ratings, pros and cons, use our [DHM supplement reviews](/reviews), or compare two directly in the [comparison tool](/compare). Whichever you choose, check with a pharmacist if you take other medicines.

On current pricing, NusaPure and Double Wood offer 1,000 mg of DHM per serving for well under a dollar, and DHM Depot is a good low-dose option. No Days Wasted is the most complete combination formula if you want added L-cysteine and electrolytes. Prices change, so compare the current listing.

faq.question: How much DHM should I take?
faq.answer: There is no established human dose. Most products give 300 mg or 1,000 mg per serving, and the one controlled human trial of DHM capsules we have found used 600 mg a day. Start at 300 mg, stay within the label, and check with a doctor or pharmacist if you take other medicines.

faq.question: Does DHM really work for hangovers?
faq.answer: The research is promising but limited. Most of it comes from rodent and lab studies, including a 2012 UCLA rat study on alcohol intoxication. The best human trial so far looked at liver markers in people with fatty liver disease, not hangovers. There is no good evidence from large human trials that DHM reliably reduces hangover symptoms, though many users report it helps.

faq.question: Is it safe to take a DHM supplement with alcohol?
faq.answer: DHM appears to be well tolerated in studies so far, and side effects reported are usually mild, such as stomach upset or drowsiness. Long-term human safety data is limited. Talk to a doctor or pharmacist first if you take sedatives, sleep medicines, blood thinners, or drugs processed by the liver, or if you are pregnant or have liver disease. DHM does not make it safe to drive after drinking.

faq.question: Is Hovenia dulcis extract the same as DHM?
faq.answer: No. Hovenia dulcis (Japanese raisin tree) extract contains DHM along with many other compounds, and labels often don't say how much DHM is inside. Most commercial DHM comes from vine tea (Ampelopsis grossedentata). If you want a known dose, choose a product that lists dihydromyricetin in milligrams on the supplement facts panel.

faq.question: Where can I buy DHM supplements?
faq.answer: DHM is sold mainly online, through Amazon and brand websites, and is less common in US pharmacies and grocery stores. Buy from the brand's official listing, check the expiry date, and compare products by price per 100 mg of DHM rather than price per bottle.

faq.question: Can you take DHM every day?
faq.answer: The longest controlled human use we know of is a three-month trial in people with fatty liver disease, at 600 mg a day. There is no long-term safety data beyond that. If you are considering daily use, talk to your doctor, especially if you take other medicines or have a liver condition.
